chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the evening journey (dulgah) to Mecca during the days of Mina, while I intended to visit the House. He said: 'No, until the dawn breaks, out of dislike that the man should spend the night without being in Mina.'

And there is no harm if a man comes during the days of Mina to Mecca and visits the House voluntarily as long as he wishes, and the best is to stay there until the end of the days of Tashriq. Narrated.

key_terms.أَيَّامَ مِنًى: The days of Mina (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.اَلتَّشْرِيق: The days of Tashriq (11th-13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.اَلدُّلْجَة: Evening journey or travel after midday
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَة: Dislike or mild aversion in jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on traveling from Mina to Mecca for voluntary visitation during the days of Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the fiqh of moving between Mina and Mecca during Hajj, distinguishing between the disliked timing for departure (before dawn) and the permissibility of voluntary Kaaba visitation. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the temporal boundaries of Mina’s stay, linking the physical act of travel to the spiritual discipline of completing the prescribed rites before engaging in optional worship.
